output.answer: Twitter (now X) has no standalone valuation today. Its last hard standalone price was set on March 28, 2025, when Elon Musk's AI company xAI acquired X in an all-stock deal valuing X at $33 billion in equity ($45 billion including $12 billion of debt), up from the $44 billion Musk paid in 2022 but far above the ~$12.5 billion Fidelity had marked it at in 2024. On February 2, 2026 SpaceX completed an all-stock acquisition of xAI — with X folded inside it — at a combined value of roughly $1.25 trillion, and SpaceX went public in June 2026; its shares now trade as SPCX with an intraday market cap of about $1.94 trillion as of November 11, 2026. No current standalone figure for X is published, but one widely shared analyst estimate puts X's implied value post-IPO at roughly $116 billion — an estimate, not a company-confirmed number.
caveats: There is no current standalone valuation for X: it is a private subsidiary (of SpaceX Super Intelligence, itself under SpaceX), and the $33 billion figure is from March 2025 and reflects a deal price between two companies under Musk's common control, not a market price.

The ~$116 billion implied X value is a back-of-envelope analyst estimate (assuming X is worth 29% of xAI and xAI 20% of a $2 trillion SpaceX), not an official figure, and others argue the platform cannot be separated from the AI business that way.

SpaceX's stock moves daily: SPCX listed at $135 in June 2026, peaked at $225.64, traded as low as $104.83, and its intraday market cap was about $1.94 trillion on November 11, 2026 — so any implied value for X moves with it.

X no longer reports its own financials; its results are folded into SpaceX's 'Super Intelligence' segment (Q3 2026 segment revenue of $7.56 billion), so segment-level figures do not isolate Twitter/X's standalone worth.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk's xAI acquired X (Twitter) in an all-stock deal that valued X at $33 billion in equity, or $45 billion including $12 billion of debt, while valuing xAI at $80 billion.

SpaceX completed an all-stock acquisition of xAI (and with it X) on February 2, 2026; the combined company was expected to price an IPO at a valuation of about $1.25 trillion, after xAI was valued at about $230 billion in a $20 billion round closed in January 2026.
SpaceX (ticker SPCX), which now owns X, traded with an intraday market cap of $1.935 trillion (previous close $143.09; 52-week range $104.83-$225.64) as of November 11, 2026.

SpaceX completed its IPO in June 2026 — the largest first-time share sale on record, raising about $75 billion ($85.7 billion with the overallotment) at roughly a $2 trillion debut valuation; the stock listed at $135 and peaked at $225.64.

X Corp. has been a wholly owned subsidiary of SpaceX Super Intelligence (formerly xAI) since March 28, 2025, and that entity has been a subsidiary of SpaceX since February 2, 2026 — X Corp. reports no valuation of its own.

Analyst estimate (not company-confirmed): assuming X is worth 29% of xAI and xAI 20% of SpaceX's post-IPO value, X's implied valuation is about $116 billion — a 3.5x return from the $44 billion 2022 take-private.
Historical mark: by late 2024 Fidelity had cut its valuation of X's equity to roughly $12.5 billion (a ~79% cut from the $44 billion purchase price), the low point before the 2025 recovery.

missing_fields: Current standalone market valuation of Twitter/X — none exists or is published; X is a private subsidiary inside SpaceX, and the most recent standalone figure is the $33 billion March 2025 deal price.
